newsitem.title: USA: Lexmark comfortable with analysts estimates.
newsitem.headline: Lexmark comfortable with analysts estimates.

text.p: Lexmark International Group Inc said Monday it expected to match analysts' earnings projections for the full year, despite reporting flat revenues in the second quarter.
"We are comfortable with the current range of analyst estimates for full-year earnings per share," said chief executive Marvin Mann in a statement.
The company did not give the range of estimates, but a First Call consensus estimate of five brokers put the company's full-year earnings at $1.98 a share.
The manufacturer of printers reported second-quarter earnings of $34.3 million, or $0.45 a share, compared with a net of $30.8 million, or $0.40 a share, the year before.
A First Call consensus estimate of five brokers had put the company's second-quarter earnings at $0.42 a share.
Lexmark's revenues of $556.3 million for the quarter were basically flat from last year's $555.3 million.
"Revenues, operating income and earnings were affected by lower prices and price protection on our predecessor printers," Mann said.

The company said it reduced prices on its predecessor Optra printer, which accounted for the majority of network laser printers it sold in the second quarter, in response to competitors cutting prices on their laser printers by 20 percent.

Lexmark also said a strong dollar and drop in revenues from other office imaging products negatively affected its revenues. It attributed the rise in net earnings to reducing products costs and sustained growth of printer sales.
The company said it expected its new Optra S network laser printers to increase printer sales and "drive profit growth from consumables."

The company said it bought back 1.14 million shares for about $27 million at prices ranging from $21.25 to $24.88 in the quarter. It added it recently implemented a new repurchase program to buy back an additional $150 million of its common stock.
